With Sunday Ogwuche participating from NOSDRA, the JIV was declared inconclusive as the community representatives do not accept the cause of spill as sabotage as declared by other state holders. Consultations has been conducted in that regards on the 13th February, 2018 with Nwanni Vincent participated from NOSDRA. On the 14th day of April the section of the facility (specimen) was removed from site for further test and examination with Madu Henry participated from NOSDRA. On the 24th day of April, 2018, the existing clamp on the specimen was removed before all the stake holders and was confirmed a pin hole at 12 o’clock on the facility and the JIV was concluded.

descriptionofimpact:
On arrival at the site on the 13th of August 2019, the JIV team discovered a raging fire emanating from the pipeline. The firefighters in the company of the JIV team was able to put out the fire after much battle.

On the 14th of August 2019, the JIV team returned to the site at about 12 noon and during the investigation, it was discovered that the pipeline was vandalized by unknown person(s) at an 11 O’clock position and there were visible signs of hacksaw marks.

Windrows were made to achieve a higher surface area for aeration.
The windrows were later removed and the soil levelled which marked the end of the remediation process.

The windrows were later removed and the soil levelled which marked the end of the remediation process.

descriptionofimpact:

•	The impacted area covered TOTALENERGIES’s Right of Way and adjoining vegetation (Third Party Area) see figure 4.

sitelocationname: 18” Kolocreek -Gbaran CPF @ Fandud Onopa Community in Yenagoa LGA, Bayelsa State.
descriptionofimpact:
i.	There was a pool of water with light crude on its surface at the incident point. 
ii.	Upon bailing of the water and manual excavation, a 3” Valve installed at 12 O’ Clock position on the pipeline was seen with a 2” galvanized pipe connected to the valve through an elbow. The 2” galvanized pipe extended to an unknown destination though suspected to be the illegal bunkering camp where the explosion occurred
iii.	While the excavation was on going, the JIT noticed smoke in the suspected illegal bunkering site which prompted the JIT to conduct the JIV without properly exposing the entire circumference of the pipe.
iv.	Due to security concerns, the JIT was disallowed from extending the investigation to the illegal bunkering site where the explosion occurred.
v.	Free phase crude oil was seen within and outside the right of way. The JIT followed the plume of crude oil to some areas with burnt vegetation. It was suspected that the fire emanated from the camp and extended toward the pipeline right of way, though the pipeline right of way was not affected by the fire.

sitelocationname: Nembe Creek Crude Oil Export Terminal, Nembe LGA Bayelsa State.
descriptionofimpact:
i.	The incident point as shown to the JIT was a manifold without any connection to the storage facility as the ruptured hose was removed before the visit.
ii.	Five (5nos) barrels of crude oil recovered before the visit was sighted stored in GP Tank.
iii.	There was no free phase oil on the platform.
iv.	The company said they dismounted the ruptured hose because they wanted to protect the environment.
v.	The river boom was poorly mounted as there were loose ends. Due to the tidal nature of the water body the booming was not effective.
vi.	There are plumes of heavy impact of crude seen within the proximity of the export terminal.
vii.	The spill impacted mangroves and shorelines within and around the coastal communities.

descriptionofimpact:
The Agency got a report of the incident on the 14th September, 2024 and called the operator to verify the alleged oil spill on Nembe Well 13 Wellhead. The Company later mobilized for JIV on the 19th of September, 2024.  Addressing the JIT the company representative explained that the incident was at Well 35 and not Well 13 as it was previously reported by the representatives of Nembe Community.

i.	The incident point at the Well 35 Wellhead showed evidence of sabotage as the maintenance team listed the parts of the well head that was vandalized and taken away as follows;
a.	2 pieces 2’’/9’’/16’’ gate/seat/bonnet/blind
b.	2 pieces of 2’’/1’’/16’’ gate/seat/bonnet/blind flanges on s/s outlet
c.	4 pieces of 2’’ blind flanges/bull plugs with ½’’ KTV on annuls A/B of both arms.
d.	18 pieces of 7/8 studs and nuts.
e.	6 pieces of RX24 ring gaskets.
f.	1 piece of KTV on tree cap.
ii.	As at the time of JIV, there were emission of gases on the Well 35 wellhead this limited the JIT from getting too close to the wellhead.
iii.	There were visible sheen and light crude on the surface of the water body.
iv.	The JIT observed that there were no security/surveillance camp within and around the wellhead.

descriptionofimpact:
: Surfer boat (Silver Line 3) reported a sheen around Eku
B wellhead platform (WHP). The sheen was traced to oily
water overflowing from a drip pan beneath the export
pipeline shutdown valve (SDV). The drip pan, which
contained residual oil, was suspected to have filled up due to
recent heavy downpours. Accumulated rainwater displaced

descriptionofimpact:
15.The following were observed during the inspection/investigation;
i.The incident point was surrounded with a containment boom with free phase crude contained inside. 
ii.During the initial assessment, the JIT with the Community representatives confirmed that there is no recent excavation at the incident point.
iii.After excavation, the JIT saw a 2’’ valve installed at 12 o’clock position on the 10’’ delivery line and the JIT confirmed third-party to be the cause of the spill.
iv.There was a collapsible containment tank stationed at the spill site with about 10 bbls inside as at JIV. 
v.The roots of mangroves were impacted to the point of water level at high tide.
vi.Aside inside the containment boom, there is no free phase crude seen within and around the spill site.

of oil sheen passing by the platform.  Sheen was observed to be 
located between Edop PP and Inim PP and heading northwards

initialcontainmentmeasures: other: 1) Platform instrumentation was isolated and drained, leak stopped. 2) Surfer carried out mechanical agitation of the water surface to  disperse the sheen
descriptionofimpact:
Operations and Maintenance personnel visited Mfem
A following a suspected sheen reported by VMT Security. The platform 
was found shut in. The test separator was observed full, resulting in 
liquid carryover to the instrumentation and drips to the sea. A pinhole 
leak was also observed on the 1-inch instrument gas line supplying the 
export pipeline and well switches.
